title: SAT Adaptive Modules: How the Two-Stage Test Really Works
summary: Why the Digital SAT's module-1-decides-module-2 design changes your strategy — and how to play it.

nodes.label: Module 2
nodes.note: Harder or easier, based on module 1

nodes.label: Score ceiling
nodes.note: The harder module 2 unlocks top scores

nodes.label: Move within a module
nodes.note: Flag & revisit — but not across modules

chunks.heading: Module 1 routes you
chunks.body: Each section's **first module is a broad mix** of easy, medium and hard questions. Your performance on it decides whether **module 2 is the harder ('higher') form or the easier ('lower') form** — and only the harder form lets you reach the top of the scale. So **module 1 is the most important stretch of the test**.
chunks.realExample: Two students both get similar raw counts, but the one who did better on module 1 is routed to a harder module 2 and can score higher — because harder questions are worth more. Module 1 is where the ceiling is set.
chunks.memoryHook: Module 1 picks your module 2 — and your ceiling. It's the highest-leverage part.

chunks.heading: You can't go back a module
chunks.body: Within a module you can **skip, flag and revisit** freely, but once you **submit a module you cannot return to it**. So finish each module deliberately: answer everything, use the flag for hard ones, and **review flagged questions before the module timer ends**.
chunks.realExample: Two minutes left in module 1? Reopen your flagged questions and lock in answers — you won't get another chance once you move to module 2.
chunks.memoryHook: Free to move inside a module, never back across one. Clear your flags before submitting.

chunks.heading: Don't panic if module 2 feels hard
chunks.body: A **harder-feeling module 2 is usually good news** — it means you earned the higher form. Don't let the difficulty rattle you; steady accuracy on a hard module 2 is exactly what produces a top score.
chunks.realExample: If module 2 questions feel tougher than module 1, that's the adaptive engine rewarding your strong start — keep calm and work carefully, you're on the high-score path.
chunks.memoryHook: Harder module 2 = you're winning. Stay calm; it's the road to a top score.

chunks.heading: Practise in Bluebook to know the flow
chunks.body: Because the adaptivity and navigation are built into the **Bluebook app**, take **official Bluebook practice tests** so the module timing, the flag tool and the module-submit step are familiar. Surprises on test day cost points; rehearsal removes them.
chunks.realExample: Doing a full Bluebook practice test teaches you the rhythm — when the module timer warns you, how the flag list looks — so on test day you're executing, not learning the interface.
chunks.memoryHook: Rehearse in Bluebook. Know the timing and the flag tool before it counts.

recall.q: What determines whether SAT module 2 is the harder or easier form?
recall.a: Your performance on module 1 of that section.

recall.q: Why is module 1 the highest-leverage part of the test?
recall.a: It routes you to a harder or easier module 2, and only the harder form unlocks the top of the score scale.

recall.q: Can you return to a module after submitting it?
recall.a: No — you can move freely within a module, but once you submit it you can't go back, so clear your flags first.

recall.q: What does a harder-feeling module 2 usually mean?
recall.a: That you did well on module 1 and earned the higher-difficulty form — which is the path to a top score.

recall.q: How should you prepare for the module flow?
recall.a: Take official Bluebook practice tests so the timing, flag tool and module-submit step are familiar on test day.
